thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: detected BGP withdrawal from transit AS12345 affecting eu-central prefixes. Sudden spike in 502/504 for hosted-inference frontends starting ~6323012280.

maria: Getting several customer tickets about 502s/timeouts. Customers say requests hang then 502. Any quick observability pointers?

dan: Gateway metrics: 502 rate jumped from ~1% -> ~11.7% on eu-central edge GW pool. p95 latency +400ms. Traces show TCP retransmits and some RSTs to provider next-hop.

net-eng: Confirmed BGP withdraw from AS12345 at ~6323012280. Their session flapped and they removed prefixes to several eu-central POPs. Provider ticket opened.

irina: Can we steer traffic away from that transit? If we change local-pref to favor peer-B at the edge, we can reduce traffic through the impacted next-hop.

mike: Applied emergency BGP weight change on eu-central edge nodes:

```
set bgp neighbor 10.20.30.1 weight 50
set bgp neighbor 10.20.30.2 weight 200
```

Partial improvement: 502s down ~35% but some hosts still see the withdrawn path due to route propagation delays and dampening.

support: Repro steps from customer triage:
1) curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.eu-central.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
2) TLS completes, then gateway returns: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` with only x-gateway-id header.

Example output pasted by customer:
```
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.eu-central.example (10.1.2.3) port 443
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< x-gateway-id: gw-ec-12
```

maria: Please paste request_ids being hit so SRE can correlate logs. We'll also update status page.

support: Request ids: [req_0a1b2c3d, req_4e5f6g7h, req_9i0j1k2l]. Attached customer pcap showing dupacks and RST.

ops-bot: Correlator: those request_ids map to gw-ec-11 and gw-ec-12. Edge hosts show 15-25% packet loss to transit next-hop and many retransmits.

dan: Auth-proxy logs show auth checks timing out mid-handshake for some flows; gateway maps upstream timeout to 502. Sequence: client -> gw (TLS ok) -> auth-proxy (timeout) -> gw returns 502.

irina: Short-term mitigation: bump auth-proxy timeout and enable retry-on-timeout at gateway for idempotent preflight checks. That should convert transient route-induced timeouts into retries.

mike: Pushed config: auth-proxy timeout 2s -> 6s in eu-central pool; gateway retry=2 for preflight. Early metrics show 502 rate falling further to ~3.2%.

net-eng: Provider says withdraw was due to an accidental config rollback; they will re-announce prefixes in ~18m and monitor.

support: CS updated affected enterprise accounts with ETA and provided retry/backoff guidance. Some customers raised concerns about billing because retries may inflate usage.

maria: Escalating to P1 due to multiple paying customers impacted. Notifying lead-ops and product.

lead-ops: Acknowledged. We'll stand up a coordination call if provider hasn't re-announced in 15m. Request a postmortem covering routing controls, detection, and billing policy for retries.

dan: Still seeing a class of failures correlated with cross-AZ hairpin where traffic gets steered back through the impacted POP. Will enable cross-AZ fallback for gateway control-plane to avoid hairpin.

mike: Cross-AZ fallback enabled; cache warmers kicked. p95 latency trending back toward baseline.

irina: Please attach tcpdump snippet to provider ticket. Sample shows triple duplicate ACKs, then server RST.

support: PCAP and request logs attached to provider ticket and CS notified. Wrote a short repro + triage note for support playbook.

ops-bot: Monitoring: 5xx trending down. Current: 5xx = 0.9% (was 11.7%), p95 latency ~120ms. Marking "mitigations in place". Will update at +30m.

maria: Thanks team. Post-incident follow-ups: root cause = provider BGP withdrawal; mitigations = route preference change, auth-proxy timeout bump, cross-AZ fallback; customer impact = transient 502s for hosted-inference in eu-central; actions = improve automated failover, update runbook, billing credit policy.

net-eng: Provider re-announced prefixes at ~6323013000. Local route dampening delayed forwarding; we flushed dampening timers and traffic restored across all edge hosts.

dan: Final check shows gateways back to normal error rates. We'll roll back emergency weights and timeouts once stable.

support: CS will coordinate any billing credits for affected customers and send final customer comms after postmortem.

maria: Incident owner assigned: maria. Postmortem author & ETA 72h. Closing active updates here. :white_check_mark:
